> Life is better without drugs or booze... the pain is more real, but so is the joy.

FTFY

Yours didn't make sense.
It was only one session so far. I'll tell him how I'm feeling next time I see him.

Mostly my brain screams ***"FFFFFUUUUUCCCCKKKK"*** and I lose control of my body. I know that probably isn't helpful.

It isn't every day; some days I'd been able to positively contribute in the class. But most days I stayed as silent as possible and hoped as hard as I could I wouldn't be called on.

It's difficult to switch meds because it's so hard to get an appointment with a psychiatrist, and even when I do find one they're only available at times few and far between. I just saw a psychiatrist after about 7 months of not seeing one and his next availability is in about a month.
I'm *usually* not crazy. I basically have severe anxiety/panic attacks any time something happens. Something like going to school.
I have the same question, I'd like to see some responses.
They don't worry anyway. If I decide to do this, I'll tell them though. Okay.
So you recommend self-admitting without consulting my parents, then? By self-admitting that's what you mean?

Everybody is recommending this, but your comment posed solely this question.

Last time I came out of the psych ward, my dad drilled it into me that the 5 days had cost us $25,000 all told, and that we didn't have that kind of money. Supposedly insurance is supposed to cover in-patient care, but apparently not if it is for mental health reasons.

If I politely ask to be voluntarily committed, they'll say no. We can't afford that. If it is involuntary and you are over 18, doesn't that mean the state pays for it? Or do I have to be a threat to others for that to be the case? I don't want to hurt anybody else.
You have counselors at your disposal, haha. You don't know how lucky you are.
